subject.title: fix(googlechat): media downloads can grow unbounded without a size cap

question: Should the exported Google Chat media helper fail closed at the documented 20 MiB default when direct callers omit `maxBytes`?
rationale: The patch fixes a real unbounded buffering path, but omitted `maxBytes` changes from uncapped to fail-closed, so maintainers should intentionally accept that API compatibility tradeoff before landing.

options.title: Accept the 20 MiB helper cap
options.body: Land this patch with the documented Google Chat media default and require direct callers that need larger media to pass an explicit `maxBytes`.

options.title: Pause for a different helper contract
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want omitted `maxBytes` to keep another public meaning and ask for that contract to be documented and tested first.

recommendation.title: Accept the 20 MiB helper cap
recommendation.body: Land this patch with the documented Google Chat media default and require direct callers that need larger media to pass an explicit `maxBytes`.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the cap-alignment commit and already framed the PR as ready for the serialized landing slot after proof.
